_why: The assembler exists to make five recorded hand-assembly mistakes unrepeatable, so each of those has a mutation restoring it. The rest defend the two things that are judgement rather than default -- the stated counts and the wiring pin -- and the task slicer, where truncating or over-running a task body ships the wrong scope with no visible error. Every mutation is born pinned to the one test it is aimed at.

mutations.name: default-the-missing-counts
mutations._mechanism: The judgement the row explicitly carves out. A default decides whether an immediate pass is a guard or a weakened test.
mutations.find: elif phase == "red" and (expect_fail is None or expect_pass is None):

mutations.name: treat-zero-counts-as-absent
mutations._mechanism: `--expect-pass 0` is a real answer. A falsy test would refuse a correct dispatch and read as strictness.
mutations.find: elif phase == "red" and (expect_fail is None or expect_pass is None):
mutations.replace: elif phase == "red" and (not expect_fail or not expect_pass):

mutations.name: hardcode-a-model-into-the-block
mutations._mechanism: A pin emitted here outranks the codex CLI's own config, so the model the TUI shows and the model 5d/5e actually runs drift apart silently — the block still looks right and the dispatch still passes.

mutations.name: drop-the-model-and-effort-overrides
mutations._mechanism: Without the override channel there is no escape hatch when the CLI's configured model cannot execute tools (gpt-5.6-luna fails as a well-formed STATUS: BLOCKED), and every explicit --model/--effort is silently discarded.

mutations.name: skip-the-interpreter-probe
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 2. A bare python3 is 3.14 here and the independent re-run errors instead of measuring.

mutations.name: probe-always-passes
mutations._mechanism: A detector that cannot fail makes every interpreter refusal vacuous -- the accept direction of the same guard.

mutations.name: allow-the-read-only-sandbox
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 4. Kills pytest's tempdir, so the run passes without measuring anything.

mutations.name: drop-the-scope-warning
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 5. Without it the agent widens the run and collects the sibling project. NOTE: the first version of this mutation was a SYNTAX ERROR, so pytest died at collection and the run was credited as `killed by its named test` -- a FAKE KILL, caught only once scoring started requiring the named test to actually fail.
mutations.find:
"That path is the scope. Do not widen it — an unscoped run collects the "
        "sibling project and dies on pre-existing errors."

mutations.name: stop-the-task-body-at-any-heading
mutations._mechanism: A task whose body has its own sub-heading would be truncated at the first one, silently shipping half a task.
mutations.find: starts = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if _TASK_RE.match(ln)]
mutations.replace: starts = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith("#")]

mutations.name: let-the-task-body-run-past-the-next-task
mutations._mechanism: The dispatch would carry the following tasks too, so the agent implements out of scope. Since `_body_end` landed, this bound only bites on a plan that MIXES heading levels (a `### Task 2` under a `## Task 1` is deeper, so the heading bound reads it as Task 1's own sub-heading) — which is why the killer test is the mixed-level one and not the same-level slicing test that used to name it.
mutations.find: next_task = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)

mutations.name: accept-a-wiring-task-with-no-pin
mutations._mechanism: Nothing downstream can see the wire; 5e would establish GREEN for a connection with no load-bearing test.
mutations.find:
if not meta["pin"]:
            raise Halt("no_wire_pin", f"task={task_id}")

mutations.name: gate-a-wiring-task-on-counts
mutations._mechanism: Counts cannot gate a wiring task -- the RED split returns identically whether or not the wire exists.

mutations.name: drop-the-residual-slot-preflight
mutations._mechanism: A raw <INLINE_...> reaching the agent reads as an unfilled template and is silently discounted.

mutations.name: preflight-matches-bare-prose-slot-names
mutations._mechanism: Prose names a slot bare; only a real slot is bracketed. Matching bare names refuses every assembly against the shipped template.

mutations.name: emit-the-same-phase-directive-for-both
mutations._mechanism: The template carries BOTH RED and GREEN instructions; without the stamp the agent picks.
mutations.find: "green": "**THIS DISPATCH IS PHASE 5e (GREEN).** Make the failing tests "
mutations.replace: "green": "**THIS DISPATCH IS PHASE 5d (RED).** Make the failing tests "

mutations.name: narrow-the-residual-preflight
mutations._mechanism: A slot with a typo or lowercase evades an `[A-Z_]+` pattern and reaches the agent as a broken prompt with no refusal at all.

mutations.name: unquote-the-interpolated-paths
mutations._mechanism: A path with a space becomes two shell arguments and the pasted block silently runs the wrong thing.

mutations.name: proceed-after-a-failed-dispatch
mutations._mechanism: The block would read a missing --out file and run pytest anyway, turning a dispatch that never ran into a verdict-shaped nothing.
mutations.find: 'if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo "dispatch failed rc=$rc" >&2; exit "$rc"; fi',

mutations.name: the-last-task-swallows-the-trailing-section
mutations._mechanism: Bounding on the next TASK header alone runs the last task to EOF. Measured over the corpus 2026-08-26: 19 of 20 impl-plans, 746 lines, up to 257 of changelog and cross-task verification pasted into one task's TDD prompt.

mutations.name: a-deeper-sub-heading-ends-the-task
mutations._mechanism: `<=` becoming `<` is wrong in the other direction: an equal-level heading no longer ends the body. `<` alone would keep the old bug for `## Version History` after a `## Task`.
mutations.find: if found is not None and found <= level:

mutations.name: a-fence-comment-truncates-the-task
mutations._mechanism: Impl-plans are full of shell blocks whose comments start at column 0, so `# do the thing` inside one would cut the task off at its own example — the same reason section_bounds in h_mad_version_history.py tracks fences.

mutations.name: a-task-header-level-is-guessed-instead-of-read
mutations._mechanism: A hardcoded level 3 bounds a `## Task` as if it were `###`, so the task's own `### Sub-heading` reads as equal-level and ends the body. The discriminating test is the SUB-HEADING one: `test_a_higher_level_heading_ends_a_deeper_task` passes under this mutant (`##` is <= 3 either way) and named it a survivor, which is a weak-test result, not a missing guard.

mutations.name: module-path-goes-verbatim-into-the-filename
mutations._mechanism: J34 restored. Every module in HemaSuite is `tools/...` and every module in this repo is `h-mad/scripts/...`, so the DEFAULT invocation halts with prompt_unwritable on a directory nobody created -- the stager unusable in both projects that run h-mad, with a hand-passed --prompt/--out/--log as the standing workaround.

mutations.name: sanitisation-leaks-into-the-prompt-body
mutations._mechanism: The one way this fix is WORSE than the bug it replaces. The module path in the prompt is the instruction Codex acts on; sanitise it there and the implementer is aimed at `tools_thing.py`, a file that does not exist -- a loud halt traded for a silent wrong edit. Mutated at the CALL SITE, not inside the helper: the helper is correct, and the whole risk of this fix is applying it to the wrong value.

_why_not_write_before_halt: A `write-the-prompt-before-the-halt` mutation was written and REMOVED as equivalent, recorded here so a later reader does not re-add it. In `main()` the prompt write sits after the `except Halt: return 2`, and `filled` does not exist before `assemble()` returns -- so a halt structurally cannot reach the write and there is no mutant that makes it. The property 'a halt writes no prompt' is guaranteed by order, not by a guard, and TestCli::test_a_halt_exits_two_and_writes_no_prompt asserts it directly. An equivalent mutant reports as `survived`, which is byte-identical to a real coverage gap.
